# dsh-macos-notifications

A Host plugin for **DeepSeek Harness** that posts **native macOS notifications** through
Notificatio

n Center. Clicking a banner brings the Harness window to the front — the
same "take me back" behavio
ur the Dock-attention plugin gives its bouncing icon.

The plugin runs inside the Host process (the Node runtime behind the Desktop app),
watches the durab

le `session/event` feed, and hands every alert to a bundled native
helper, **DSH Notify**. It never
writes to the session log and never talks to the model.
## Why a native helper

`osascript`'s `display notification` belongs to the script runner: the banner has no
app identity of

its own, so clicking it can only focus the script editor (or reveal it
in Finder). The helper is a

tiny `LSUIElement` app that posts the banner through
`UNUserNotificationCenter` under its own bundle

id. macOS then routes the click back to
the helper, which activates DeepSeek Harness (or launches i

t, when it is not running)
and quits.

The helper is copied once to
`~/Library/Application Support/dsh-macos-notifications/DSH Notify.app`

— quarantine
flag stripped, ad-hoc signed, registered with LaunchServices — and launched with
`open

-n -g`, so posting a banner never steals focus and the notification permission
survives plugin updat

es. Request files and the helper log live next to it in
`runtime/`.

The banner wears the **DeepSeek Harness icon**: the banner shows the icon of the app
that posted it,

so on install the plugin extracts `icon.icns` from the installed
Harness app, writes it into the he

lper bundle and signs it. Nothing third-party is
shipped in the repository; if Harness is not instal

led the configured
`targetBundleId` app's icon is used, and otherwise the generic app icon.
## What triggers a notification
| Moment | Default | Notification |

| A turn finished | on | `Turn finished` / `Ход завершён` |
| A turn failed | on | `Turn failed` + t

he error message |
| A turn hit the token limit | on | `Token limit reached` |
| An approval is requ

ested | on | `Approval needed · <tool>` |
| The agent asks a question (`ask_user_question`, `exit_pl
an_mode`) | on | `Your answer is needed · <question>` |

User-cancelled turns (`aborted`), forked and interrupted turns are silent. Subagent
sessions are ign

ored so only the sessions you actually see can ring the bell. The
notification body carries the sess

ion title (or, before a title exists, the workspace
folder name).
## Configuration
Every field is optional; the row's `config` mapping is merged over these defaults.
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `language` | `auto` | `en`, `ru`, or `auto` (host locale). |
| `sound` | `Glass` | macOS system so

und name or an absolute audio path; `null` for a silent banner. |
| `notifyOnTurnEnd` | `true` | Not

ify when a turn completes, fails, or is blocked. |
| `notifyOnApproval` | `true` | Notify when the a

gent waits for an approval decision. |
| `notifyOnQuestion` | `true` | Notify when the agent asks th

e user a question. |
| `targetBundleId` | `com.deepseek.dsh` | App a banner click activates. Point i

t at your browser's bundle id when you run `dsh web` in a browser. |
| `openUrl` | `dsh://open` | Op
ened by the helper when `targetBundleId` is not installed. |

The configured sound is played by the plugin itself while the banner stays silent, so
custom system
sound names (`Glass`, `Ping`, …) keep working.

## macOS permission

The first banner triggers a system prompt — **"DSH Notify" Would Like to Send You
Notifications**. C

lick **Allow**, and the waiting banner is posted immediately. The
answer is cached per bundle id, so

the waiting banner is posted immediately. The
answer is cached per bundle id, so this happens once.

The helper waits up to two minutes for the answer; if you miss the prompt, open
**System Settings →

Notifications → DSH Notify** and enable notifications. Without
permission no banners appear, and the

helper log says
`authorization denied; the user must allow notifications for DSH Notify`.

## Updating and moving

A `file:` row is not watched by HMR, because the file lives outside the profile
directory. After edi

ting `index.js`, touch `cordis.patch.yml` or restart the app so the
module is imported again. Moving

or deleting the checkout breaks a `file:` or `link:`
install; reinstall the bundle from the new pat

ng the checkout breaks a `file:` or `link:`
install; reinstall the bundle from the new path instead.
## Troubleshooting

- **No banners at all** — check **System Settings → Notifications → DSH Notify**; the
first run asks

for permission and the answer is cached. The helper log lives at
`~/Library/Application Support/dsh

-macos-notifications/runtime/helper.log`.
- **Clicking a banner does nothing / opens Finder** — that

is the pre-1.1.0
`osascript` build (banners belong to the script runner). Update to 1.1.0+, where t

he
banner belongs to DSH Notify and the click activates Harness.
